sections.5:
Archlin operates in specialty chemicals manufacturing with SAP S/4HANA as its ERP system and an Excel-based planning process as the current planning tool. In the current state, Archlin’s demand planners spend significant time consolidating forecasts from multiple regions, and there is no centralized planning platform across North America and Europe. Forecast accuracy is approximately 68%, inventory levels are higher than target due to poor forecast visibility, and manual Excel processes create delays in monthly planning cycles. Collaboration between sales, operations, and supply chain teams is a stated challenge, and business users have emphasized the need for collaborative forecasting and visibility across regions. Within the Phase 1 supply management scope, these conditions directly affect Archlin’s ability to improve inventory planning, identify raw material shortages in a timely manner, and maintain a single source of planning data.

The proposed solution for Archlin is to implement Kinaxis RapidResponse for Demand Planning, Supply Planning, and Inventory Optimization, supported by required interfaces from SAP S/4HANA and related planning data sources. The solution is expected to generate statistical baseline forecasts, support planner forecast overrides, track forecast history and changes, and support multiple forecast hierarchies. It will also allow sales teams to provide forecast input, enable approval workflows, provide forecast comparison reports, and deliver dashboard-based reporting. For supply planning, the solution will generate constrained supply plans, identify material shortages, support capacity planning, provide exception-based alerts, and enable scenario analysis. For inventory planning, the solution will define safety stock policies, calculate inventory targets, monitor excess inventory, track inventory turns, and optimize stock across locations.

<IMAGE id="7ef1d941d124"/>

Archlin’s implementation will require integration of the planning platform with the specified planning interfaces, including Product Master, Customer Master, Sales Orders, Inventory Balances, Purchase Orders, and Production Orders. The data refresh frequency is defined as every 4 hours, supporting more timely planning visibility than the current Excel-based monthly planning cycle. These interfaces are critical for enabling a centralized planning environment where demand, supply, and inventory signals can be evaluated together, rather than being consolidated manually across regions. The implementation approach should therefore focus on establishing a reliable planning data foundation, enabling planners to use automated forecast generation with controlled manual overrides, and configuring exception-based visibility for recurring raw material shortage issues highlighted by supply planners.

The target operating model for Archlin will move planning execution from manual spreadsheet consolidation toward a single source of planning data. Demand planners will be able to compare forecasts, review forecast accuracy and bias, track MAPE by product family, and apply market-driven overrides where needed. Sales input and approval workflows will support cross-functional collaboration, while supply planners will use constrained supply plans, shortage identification, capacity planning support, and scenario analysis to evaluate feasible supply responses. Inventory planners will use safety stock policies, inventory targets, excess inventory monitoring, inventory turns tracking, and stock optimization across locations to address the stated issue of inventory levels being higher than target due to poor forecast visibility.

The expected outcomes for Archlin are aligned to the documented success criteria. Forecast accuracy is targeted to be greater than 85%, inventory reduction is targeted to be greater than 15%, and planning cycle reduction is targeted to be greater than 30%. Additional success criteria include improved planner productivity and establishment of a single source of planning data. Leadership expects measurable improvements in forecast accuracy and inventory reduction within six months of go-live. These outcomes will be enabled by replacing fragmented Excel-based processes with centralized planning, improving visibility across regions, supporting collaborative forecasting, and giving planners exception-based insight into shortages, excess inventory, inventory targets, and constrained supply plans.
